Continents were already wired this way by 1872.

script.spoken: Your internet depends on hidden seabed cables. Deep-sea sections are only about 25 millimetres across. They weigh around 1.4 tonnes per kilometre on the seabed. Continents were already wired this way by 1872. When one breaks, a cable ship must find the fault and splice it at sea. Until then, traffic reroutes onto other cables, if they have room. So repair ships are part of the internet too.
